identity.title: GRB 980425 host: [C II], [O I], and CO lines reveal recent enhancement of star formation due to atomic gas inflow

paper_type_evidence.quote: We obtained the first ever far-infrared (FIR) line observations of a GRB host, namely Herschel/PACS resolved [C II] 158 μm and [O I] 63 μm spectroscopy, as well as APEX/SHeFI CO(2-1) line detection and ALMA CO(1-0) observations

evidence.quote: GRB 980425 at $z=0.0085$ is at a luminosity distance of 36.5 Mpc and $1''$ corresponds to 175 pc at its redshift.

question.value: Is star formation in the GRB 980425 host fuelled by a recent inflow of atomic gas, as probed by FIR line, CO and SFR indicators?

evidence.quote: Our aim is to test this possibility by studying in detail the properties of gas in the closest galaxy hosting a GRB (980425).

claims.hypothesis: GRB host star formation was recently enhanced by atomic gas inflow
claims.result: Line SFRs 1.5-6 times above IR SFR; high [OI]/FIR; low CO
claims.finding: Consistent with very recent atomic gas inflow

evidence.quote: consistent with the hypothesis of a very recent (at most a few tens of Myr ago) inflow of atomic gas triggering star formation

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Low metallicity, end of star formation episode, and minor merger considered less likely

evidence.quote: Here we provide arguments that alternative explanations for our data are less likely.

limitations_admitted.value: ALMA CO(1-0) flux of the host underestimated if extended emission present

evidence.quote: if such emission is present, then our CO(1-0) flux of the entire host is underestimated

referee_caveats_inferred: ALMA CO is non-detection and resolves out extended emission
